assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology from gut-hormone discovery through incretin biology to drugs transforming diabetes and obesity treatment is a rare combination of originality, clarity and large, lasting clinical impact, with downstream effects on appetite-regulating brain circuits that are of general physiological interest.
assessment.attribution: Decisive discovery-stage contributions are credited to Holst (incretin physiology and GLP-1 action in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 receptor biology and the therapeutic concept) and Mojsov (peptide identification/synthesis of the active form). Knudsen is credited for the industrial development of liraglutide and semaglutide, which is plausibly a development rather than discovery contribution. Other key figures in early GLP-1 work may not be in the supplied names; I cannot verify the full credit history from memory.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: multiple independent large outcome trials and widespread clinical use over more than a decade; recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Fair allocation of credit among discovery contributors versus drug developers is disputed and unresolved.
The three-person limit forces exclusion of at least one credited name; I have not independently verified priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience a causal, cell-type-specific tool and has reshaped circuit analysis across systems from invertebrates to primates; it is highly original, and its impact on how motor and other circuits are interrogated is widely acknowledged.
assessment.attribution: Bamberg and Nagel established channelrhodopsin as a light-gated ion channel; Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal control in a way that made the method general; Hegemann and Miesenboeck made earlier or parallel decisive contributions. A fair trio is hard to define, and I chose the channelrhodopsin discovery plus the broad neuronal implementation, leaving out strong candidates.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than fifteen years of independent replication and routine use; clinical translation is early but the tool's impact is already clear.
uncertainties: Six credited names with contested priority and a three-laureate cap.
Whether recognition should favor the molecular discovery or the neuronal application is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produce durable remissions in otherwise refractory hematologic cancers and opened a new therapeutic modality; the concept and clinical proof are both strong.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed early CAR design with co-stimulation, June the clinical translation in leukemia, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early engineered-lymphocyte trials. This is a plausible fair configuration, though other contributors (e.g., Eshhar, not on the supplied list) are not available to me.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: multiple approved products and several years of long-term follow-up, though toxicity, solid-tumor limits and durability remain open.
uncertainties: Eshhar-type foundational concept credit is not in the supplied names.
Long-term durability and safety across indications still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed an organelle-to-nucleus signaling pathway and a general principle of proteostasis, with importance for secretory physiology, neurodegeneration, metabolism and cancer. It is conceptually clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently identified the core signaling steps (Ire1/Hac1-XBP1 splicing and related machinery) in a complementary way, and the two-person credit appears coherent and fair.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of confirmation across yeast and mammals; therapeutic exploitation is still developing, but the basic discovery stands on its own.
uncertainties: Whether the field is viewed as prize-ready before clear clinical translation.
Other contributors to the pathway (e.g., Ron, not listed) are not among the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation provides a synaptic cellular model of learning and memory and is foundational to modern synaptic physiology. The originality of the 1973 discovery is clear, and the concept is deeply influential, though the link to memory is partly correlative.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo made the original observation; Collingridge identified NMDA receptor dependence, a decisive mechanistic step. Morris's behavioral work tied LTP to spatial learning and is also important. A three-name selection omits one strong contributor.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with half a century of independent confirmation; recognition is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Direct causal evidence that LTP is the memory mechanism remains debated.
Choice among four credited names under a three-laureate cap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identifying TNF as a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis and proving it clinically changed the treatment of chronic inflammatory disease and showed that blocking a single cytokine can be effective.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly developed the concept and the clinical proof, which is a clean and fair two-person credit; other contributors in TNF biology and antibody engineering are not part of this candidate's supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of use across several indications and biosimilars; recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Prior Nobel recognition of antibody engineering may weigh on the committee's perceived novelty.
Credit for TNF biology versus the therapeutic concept may be viewed as split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defined how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity and is relevant for infection, autoimmunity, cancer and aging; the discovery of the second-messenger cGAMP was original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP and Barber identified STING, which are the two decisive mechanistic steps; Ishikawa is another early STING contributor and the other names are co-authors on the cGAS work.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: strong independent confirmation of the mechanism, but clinical translation is still incomplete, so recognition might be slightly early.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is not yet established.
Priority among STING discovery contributors is not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition provided the first dramatic proof of targeted kinase-inhibitor therapy in cancer, converting a fatal leukemia into a chronic condition, and set the model for molecularly targeted oncology.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical proof), Lydon (drug development) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and follow-on inhibitors) form a plausible trio, but the contributions of the underlying BCR-ABL biology (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore, not listed) is outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with two decades of survival data; recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Foundational BCR-ABL biology credit is not in the supplied names.
The prize may be seen as more translational than discovery-driven.
